status: exploratory descriptive audit of immutable completed games
hypothesis: Atomic replanning can change the intended remaining fuel bundle before another player acts, so executed turns may differ from the complete bundles valued by search.
prior_inspection: One 2p search-opponent game was inspected before this design. Its first resource turn selected two coal, bought one, then passed. This is not a preregistered confirmatory test.
scope: All 1680 resource-filter games and paired filter terminals from the completed 54-job, 3360-game screen. No new inference, games, jobs, gradients or policy selection.
primary_descriptions: For adjacent plan-bearing resource requests in the same round, compare the newly selected count vector with the preceding selected vector minus the just-executed purchase.
Separate count-vector changes from mere action reordering; also count immediate next-move deviations.
Report whether the preceding remainder was present in the new candidate menu, whether the public sampling seed changed, and the new selected-minus-remainder estimated credit when comparable.

For each resource turn containing a search, compare actual purchases through Pass with the first selected bundle, separating shortfalls, excess, mixed changes and exact completion. Forced terminal Pass without a plan is included; unsearched turns are outside this denominator.
Retain every game, count/opponent/rule cell and paired outcome category. Association with losses is descriptive, not evidence that commitment would improve outcomes.
integrity: Check input files against the existing immutable archive manifest and decision digests in game records. Check consecutive decision numbers, same-round turn closure, resource stock/market transitions and nonnegative cash. Existing complete-screen verification remains the source for rollout legality and terminal auditing.
examples: Choose minimum SHA256(identity) examples within changed-plan, early-Pass and first-bundle-shortfall categories, without ranking by outcome or estimated advantage.
interpretation: No significance claim or independent-observation interpretation for repeated decisions. This audit cannot separate Monte Carlo noise, candidate-menu changes or model inconsistency, establish causal harm, or promote a committed policy. Any redesign needs fresh paired full-game evaluation.
